main_issue: The stated mechanism is coherent and actionable, but most displayed cases provide only patch-derived review windows rather than source-to-sink evidence; the group also carries a mixed-label warning and an unsubstantiated claim of unrelated outliers.
evidence_notes: Dspace, S3Proxy, and Graylog provide concrete evidence of request- or API-controlled path components being resolved under a base directory before read/write/delete effects.

S3Proxy demonstrates the full reusable pattern particularly well: untrusted keys or prefixes reach list, read, write, and delete path resolution without normalized containment under the container root.
Dspace supports traversal through resumable upload identifiers used to construct directories and chunk paths under a temporary upload root.

Graylog supports untrusted filename flow into download/delete operations, although the supplied evidence says validation exists and does not establish whether its containment check was actually deficient pre-fix.
The remaining shown cases only establish source readiness and patch-anchor provenance, not the vulnerable source shape, sink, missing guard, or exploit condition.
Before accepting the full 18-case group, inspect the label-only cases and substantiate or remove any deserialization, SSRF, regex-injection, or XSS outliers mentioned in the cluster summary.
